check.question: Which ticket IDs had a customer message by the end of March 31, 2026, but no subsequent public human agent reply on that ticket by then?
check.sql:
WITH first_customer AS (
  SELECT e.ticket_id,
         e.occurred_at,
         e.seq,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.ticket_id ORDER BY e.occurred_at, e.seq) AS rn
  FROM ticket_messages m
  JOIN ticket_events e ON e.event_id = m.event_id
  WHERE m.author_kind = 'customer'
    AND e.occurred_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
)
SELECT fc.ticket_id
FROM first_customer fc
WHERE fc.rn = 1
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM ticket_messages r
    JOIN ticket_events re ON re.event_id = r.event_id
    JOIN agents a ON a.agent_id = r.author_agent_id
    WHERE re.ticket_id = fc.ticket_id
      AND r.author_kind = 'agent'
      AND r.visibility = 'public'
      AND r.is_automated = 0
      AND a.is_human = 1
      AND (re.occurred_at > fc.occurred_at OR (re.occurred_at = fc.occurred_at AND re.seq > fc.seq))
      AND re.occurred_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
  )
ORDER BY fc.ticket_id;

check.witness: Ticket 6001: customer message 2026-03-15 10:00 (event 60002) is followed within March only by a PRIVATE human agent note (event 60003, agent 1002, 2026-03-16 09:00) and a PUBLIC but AUTOMATED system acknowledgement (event 60004, is_automated=1, 2026-03-16 09:05); the public human reply from agent 1002 (event 60006) lands 2026-04-05, after the March cutoff. Gold includes 6001; wrong_sql drops the visibility='public' predicate and counts the private note as a qualifying reply, so it drops 6001 (wrong result: [[6005],[6006]]). Ticket 6002 (public human reply 2026-03-20, event 60009) correctly drops out of both; 6004's first customer message is 2026-04-02 (outside March) so it is excluded from both; 6005's only public human reply (event 60015, 2026-03-10) precedes its first customer message (2026-03-12) so it is included by both; 6006's only subsequent public agent reply (event 60020, 2026-03-15) is from bot agent 1004 (is_human=0) so it is included by both.
